caveats: The 1,500 orders a minute with cancels at 50 msgs/s was measured over one 20-second rung, not a full minute.
The third wire message per order (one reqAllOpenOrders per cancel) is derived from the adapter source at the pin; it was not captured on the wire.
The official client was not tested above 50 msgs/s (cap); whether the Gateway saturates between 50 and 57 is unmeasured.
Adapter rungs whose wire estimate exceeded 50 msgs/s ran above the cap in wire terms; no pacing text, no code 100 and no disconnect occurred.
The counted rate excludes the hidden request; the wire estimate is the cap-relevant figure.
Broker-side completed-order counts (6,292 and 8,494) are live raw-protocol reads recorded in the session transcript, not receipt files.
A first count attempt through a Nautilus node returned zero orders and is not used as evidence.
The pair tests T1..T10 and the reqIds probe were placed after the second independent count; a third raw-protocol count (10,313) is transcript-derived and reconciles by arithmetic (ADDENDUM-01).

Of the 38 journal orders absent at the broker, 35 carry the venue's [103] duplicate-order-id refusal, 1 a cancel-target-not-found rejection and 2 never reached the adapter (revision 2 corrects the v1 label of 36 as [103]).
Latencies of the pair tests are single 14-30 second runs at 10 msgs/s per connection and are not a latency study.
Timing offsets compare two timestamps taken on one host clock.

Per-second maxima (revision 3): whole-run, combined and per-rung-window `max_1s` / `best_5s_mean` are maxima over sliding windows anchored at a message; the revision-2 UTC-bucket values are kept as `*_utc_buckets` and are never above them.

The receipts' own per-rung `counted_msgs_per_s_min` / `counted_msgs_per_s_max` are fixed one-second slot counters, so they are bucket values and lower bounds of the sliding maximum; the official client's receipts hold no per-message times, so its per-second maxima cannot be recomputed under the sliding definition.

`peak_open_orders` of the adapter runs closes an order at its first terminal order event (revision 3); the official client's `peak_open_orders` is the probe's own run-time counter and is not recomputable from the receipts.

Per-rung wire means (revision 4) are the wire-series messages inside the rung's own window divided by its recorded seconds: they include the cancels of other rungs' orders sent in the window and exclude the cancels of the rung's own orders sent outside it, and for a rung stopped part-way they cover only its recorded seconds; the order-attributed values of revisions 1 to 3 are kept as `*_by_order_rung`.

peak_open_orders_definition.derivation: the journals' own `event` vocabulary intersected with the Nautilus terminal order events (filled, canceled, cancelled, expired, denied, rejected); order_cancel_rejected (a refused cancel) and order_pending_cancel are not terminal
peak_open_orders_definition.official_client_peak_open: source-derived from the private probe script, not recomputable: the receipts' `peak_open_orders` of the official-client runs are the probe's own run-time counter (at each placement: the orders already placed and not marked done, plus the one being placed); the probe marks an order done only on a Cancelled / ApiCancelled / Inactive status, a 202 notice or a 10147 / 10148 error, so a [103]-refused order counts as open until its stale cancel is answered; these values are unchanged in revisions 3 and 4
peak_open_orders_definition.open_until: the order's FIRST terminal order event; an order with no terminal event (an order_submitted with no later event, for one) stays open to the end of the journal
peak_open_orders_definition.partial_fills: every ladder order has quantity 1, so an order_filled event is a complete fill
peak_open_orders_definition.peak: the running count is updated at every submit and every terminal event of a rung's own orders and the rung's peak is the largest value reached; at equal timestamps terminal events are applied before submits
peak_open_orders_definition.revision_2_defect: revision 2 closed an order only at order_canceled, so a rejected, filled, expired or denied order stayed open for ever
peak_open_orders_definition.scope: adapter ladder orders (journal step S4), per rung of the receipt's ladder

rate_window_conventions.anchor: a window can always be shifted right to the first message it holds without losing one, so the maximum over every real start time equals the maximum over message-anchored windows
rate_window_conventions.best_5s_mean: the largest number of messages of the series in any half-open interval [t, t + 5 s) whose start t is the timestamp of a message of that series, divided by 5, rounded to 2 decimals

same_name_new_meaning: wire_est_upper_bound_msgs_per_s_mean (every adapter rung, and the adapter_r6_rung30/40/50 headline entries)

rate_window_conventions.interval: half-open: a message exactly 1 s (5 s) after the start is outside the window; timestamps are compared as exact integer microseconds since the Unix epoch, never as floating-point seconds
rate_window_conventions.max_1s: the largest number of messages of the series in any half-open interval [t, t + 1 s) whose start t is the timestamp of a message of that series
rate_window_conventions.official_client: the official-client receipts hold no per-message times, so their per-second maxima cannot be recomputed under the sliding definition
rate_window_conventions.receipt_slot_counters: counted_msgs_per_s_min and counted_msgs_per_s_max of a rung are the receipts' own fixed one-second slot counters (from the rung start for the adapter, integer seconds of the probe's monotonic clock for the official client): bucket values, hence lower bounds of the sliding maximum; they are unchanged
rate_window_conventions.rung_window: max_1s_sliding_in_rung_window applies the same sliding maximum to the step-S4 submit and cancel rows inside a rung's window, which starts at the S4 step_enter row's timestamp plus (rung index x the frozen rung_s) and lasts the rung's recorded seconds; it is the harness's own per-second slot grid replayed from the journal

rung_window_replay.reading: where the replay differs, one message was sent in the milliseconds between the nominal end of the previous rung and the harness tick that journalled the next rung's start; the harness does not count such a message (its slot index, 20, falls outside the finished rung's 20-slot row) and the replay counts it in the first slot of the new window

rate_window_conventions.rung_wire_means: wire_est_refined_msgs_per_s_mean and wire_est_upper_bound_msgs_per_s_mean of an adapter rung (and of the adapter_r6_rung30/40/50 headline entries) are the number of messages of that series whose journal time lies inside the rung's own window, divided by the rung's recorded seconds and rounded to 2 decimals: the same window rows and message series as max_1s_sliding_in_rung_window, the hidden reqAllOpenOrders counted as in `series`. They include the cancels of other rungs' orders that were sent inside the window and exclude the cancels (and, for a rung stopped part-way, the submits after its recorded seconds) of the rung's own orders that were sent outside it. Revisions 1 to 3 published (submits + cancels + known) / seconds with cancels and known counted over the orders the rung SUBMITTED wherever they were sent; those values are kept as wire_est_refined_msgs_per_s_mean_by_order_rung and wire_est_upper_bound_msgs_per_s_mean_by_order_rung. cancels_sent, cancels_with_known_venue_id and cancels_before_acceptance stay order-attributed (the first cancel row of each order the rung submitted); cancels_sent_in_own_window, cancels_sent_in_other_rung_window and cancels_sent_outside_rung_windows classify those same first cancel rows by journal time against every rung window of the run and sum to cancels_sent
rate_window_conventions.series: counted = one message per submit row and per cancel row; wire_est_refined and wire_est_upper_bound add the adapter's hidden reqAllOpenOrders per cancel (refined: only for a cancel of an order that had been accepted), stamped with the cancel row's timestamp because the journal does not timestamp it
rate_window_conventions.utc_buckets: max_1s_utc_buckets and best_5s_mean_utc_buckets are the revision-2 numbers: messages per UTC second (the integer second of the timestamp), the largest bucket and the best mean of 5 consecutive buckets; a sliding maximum is never below its bucket value and exceeds it when a burst straddles a second boundary

revision.reason: A co-op question on nas#1083 showed that the per-rung wire means of revisions 1 to 3 charged each rung with the cancels of the orders it SUBMITTED, wherever those cancels were sent, over the rung's own recorded seconds: a cancel sent in the next rung's window, or after the ladder, was counted in the submission rung, and for a rung stopped part-way the submits after its recorded seconds were counted too, so a rung's mean was not the rate of messages inside its window. The per-message series (max_1s_sliding_in_rung_window, the whole-run and combined rate blocks) and the official-client figures were already window or message based and are unchanged.
